scope: Removal of retired coarse-cost statistics and unused tile diagnostic counters; shared GPU plan split by ownership. Final hot update functions retain cross-module inlining availability. No GPU kernel or dispatch policy changes.

method.timing: host_submit_ms starts before transaction mutation/commit and ends after renderer submission. completed_frame_ms adds GPU completion wait. Scene/context creation, initial render, GPU readback and PNG output are outside frame timing. One frame in flight.
method.workloads: 512 rounded controls on 1280x720, one moves; 2048 controls on 3200x2000, all move; 32 controls plus a 3712x1920 panel on 4096x2160, only panel moves. Frames alternate between 0 and 16 pixel translations. All use actual RetainedScene transactions, NativeRenderer, native textures and GPU submission.

pixels.comparison: Every exploratory, warm and timed process final readback matches the unchanged baseline scene; this checks final images, not every intermediate frame.

interpretation: Final controlled-UI medians preserve application frame/submit cost; no speedup is claimed. First final series panel p95 was 8.352ms vs 6.706ms, while the prespecified replication reverses it to 6.675ms vs 7.558ms. Same-executable controls also exhibit large p95 variations (scrolling 15.945ms vs 6.631ms), so latency tails are not stable enough to attribute to this cleanup. All series/samples are retained. Existing native_present whole-process p50 changes by -0.734%; this does not isolate tile indexing or GPU throughput. Neither these controlled scenes nor window smoke establish universal workloads or DX12/Vulkan performance.

actual_native_present_application.method: Existing native_present metal --smoke application: eight frames, 640x360 to 480x270 physical resize; one warm process per executable, eight alternating timed pairs. Whole-process time includes context/window/cache initialization, GPU rendering/presentation and teardown, not isolated frame time. Metal validation disabled during timing. No concurrent build or GPU workload.
